name: The workbench shows the voice coordinator's turns and who delegated
summary: Each tab session records which voice coordinator turn delegated each workhorse turn, so the snapshot carries the coordinator's turns beside the workhorse's and the workbench marks delegated work with where it came from.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/9ncuT5DP#qTmIytbT
changes.value: A turn that delivered, steered or queued work, or whose delivery may have reached the workhorse, shows in the conversation of each workhorse it reached. A delegation the workhorse refused as busy or with an invalid body gave it nothing, and moves the turn nowhere. A turn that gave work to none shows in the conversation shown while it ran. A turn with no record shows in whatever conversation is shown. The timeline keeps only the turns of the shown conversation before it spends its budget. The tab session also subscribes a recorder to its workhorse operations. A delegate_to_workhorse event that names its workhorse turn records that turn against the coordinator turn that asked. A steer is never recorded, because it adds to a turn that the person or an earlier delegate started. The session keeps the 256 newest records, and the projection of the workhorse timeline marks a recorded turn with delegatedBy.

value.label: a delegate's workhorse turn started
value.description: Each tab session subscribes the recorder to its workhorse operations once. The started event of a delegate_to_workhorse operation names the workhorse turn and the coordinator turn that asked, and the recorder keeps that pair.

value.label: a delegate's turn, with the coordinator turn that asked
value.note: A queued delegate is recorded when its turn starts. A steer is never recorded.
